Hey everyone. So I've never been a good shot with a handgun but always thought the old pistols in western a were pretty cool. How they balance and fit your hand is a personal thing, the only way to know is to visit a gun shop and see how they feel to you. The rugers are better-made, more durable guns with excellent CS and better aftermarket support, the Italian-made guns are closer to the historic originals. Whatever floats your boat the most.

Adjustable sights vrs. fixed sights are another issue to consider. Life gets annoying if the windage is off on a fixed sight gun.

.38/.357 is less traditional, but offers plenty of power when you want it, and a wide range of softer-shooting factory loads when you don't. Compare the price of .38 and .45 Colt ammo before you decide.

In good hands these are potentially very accurate guns. You won't believe what Elmer Keith used to do with them.

There's a shop about an hour away with a bunch in stock so I guess I should go visit them to see how they feel. Thanks for the quick advice.

They come in three different barrel lengths, 7 1/2, 5 1/2, and 4, as I recall. Of course they each balance differently, and yes, the smaller bore usually means a thicker barrel, which adds a little weight up front.

The 7 1/2 was the original army issue standard, but they decided 5 1/2 was better and converted all of their guns a few years later. The 4 inch guns were the most popular with civilians - so any of them are as authentic as the others.

I have mostly Ruger and one Pietta. If Uberti I prefer the 1875. I’ve got .41 Magnum, .44 Special, .22lr, .357, and .44 ball. The .44 ball and .41 Magnum are my favorites.

Uberti makes more anachronistic guns but the only no 3 and 1875s. Buy Uberti for non-colt SA revolvers.

Pietta is bigger in cap and ball. A .36 1858 makes a good .38 Special conversion.
